parsed.explanation: The combined regime documents state-directed targeting: a 2016 police LGBTIQ register, a 2017 government registry, and 2024 police luring people to fake meetings to register them, harvest contacts and extort money (10+ cases in one province; 27 recorded violation cases nationally). Raids brought forced HIV testing, arbitrary criminal charges, and documented ill-treatment, sexual abuse and extortion by officers. No SOGI non-discrimination protection exists; the 2022 law omits both grounds; police inaction on forced/sham marriages is recorded. Society is described as entirely negative with hostile political and religious rhetoric, raising outing probability. Offsetting: same-sex relations legal since 1998, no trans-specific criminal offence, no death penalty or documented trans killings, and no recorded imprisonment for identity. Border/document exposure is unsourced, not cleared. Worst feature is tier-2 state-tolerated police targeting with no working recourse.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. The inventory explicitly does not address entry/visa rules, border or airport screening, or passport gender markers; this is an open question, not a clearance. Gender recognition in-country is near-impossible (3–6 people ever), so a visitor's foreign documents carry their own marker.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry could feed the documented police database/registration practice if referred inward; the linkage is unrecorded.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: 2022/2023 raids with arbitrary criminal charges; documented police ill-treatment, sexual abuse and extortion; 2024 cases of arbitrary arrest; entrapment to force registration. Charges appear pretextual rather than identity-statute based.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Same-sex conduct decriminalised 1998; no trans-specific offence documented; no death penalty. Courts' treatment of trans detainees unsourced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor stopped for any reason enters the same policing apparatus that runs the register and entrapment; trans detainee conditions are explicitly unsourced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: One northern province documented with 10+ entrapment/extortion cases; national register, raids and registry described as countrywide. Record warns counts are raw and not per-capita comparable.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Provincial variation cannot be used as safety: no other province is named, and the national practices cover all territory.

care_services.exposure: Documented: no gender-affirming care in country; disrespectful medical staff; pseudoscientific 'cure methods'; forced HIV testing in raids. A trans visitor needing emergency or routine care faces documented hostility.
care_services.protection: A trans NGO's HRT protocol educates some endocrinologists; a 2024 regional study includes guidance for trans migrants.
care_services.interaction: Care-seeking can expose trans status to staff within the same hostile institutional culture; insurance and refill issues are not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: police as perpetrators (registry, entrapment, extortion, sexual abuse), state registry of 'proven' LGBT persons, entirely negative public attitudes, hostile senior religious authority and politicians, suppressed public support.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Decriminalisation since 1998; anonymous LGBT NGOs exist, one trans-focused.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Institutions are the threat actor, so rule of law aggravates rather than mitigates; activists have no access to ministries, foreclosing advocacy remedy.

minors_guardians.exposure: Forced/sham marriages imposed on LGBT people with police inaction are documented (2024), a captive-family pattern a visiting minor or partner could enter. Nothing on LGBTQ minors or education is recorded.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a minor gains no documented protection; family/community hostility plus police inaction is the operative combination, but child-specific exposure is unsourced.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented: 27 recorded violation cases in 2024 (arbitrary arrest, blackmail, extortion); disclosure targets people to physical and psychological abuse including by police (2013, dated); entirely negative public attitudes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Same-sex relations legal; no documented trans killings; a regional network records and reports cases.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Raw counts without denominators limit rate inference, but the pattern is state-involved, recurring, and current (2024), so it is not a single-incident artifact.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No SOGI non-discrimination law (2022 statute keeps only 'sex', partially aligned per 2024 review); no relationship recognition; no access to state authorities; documented 'law protects but practice does not' gaps.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts and complaints are not shown to be closed, but no successful trans remedy is recorded; the first anti-discrimination statute exists though incomplete.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Oversight has recorded violations without remedying them; border treatment, registry currency and trans detention conditions remain unsourced rather than safe.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest match: police raids on a support space, forced registration, photography and extortion, with slow courts and scarce legal aid. The dossier here adds a standing state registry and entrapment harvesting contacts, but lacks 0.25-A's proposed-penalty escalation and documented short jail terms, so scores level rather than below.

Lower than 0.35-B: Karthovia's identity stops produce hours-long interviews and nuisance fines, whereas this dossier documents a police registry, forced HIV testing, arbitrary criminal charges, and sexual abuse by officers. The severity here is materially above a friction-and-fine regime.

Higher than 0.15-B: Saruth detains transgender visitors for weeks in hostile custody with capital provisions in reach. Here same-sex conduct is legal, no trans offence or death penalty is documented, no prolonged trans imprisonment is recorded, and entry rules are unsourced rather than exclusionary.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: a decriminalised but surveilled environment where the state itself manufactures discovery. Same-sex legality (1998) removes the identity offence, yet the 2016 police register, the 2017 registry, and 2024 entrapment-to-register operations make exposure an instrument of policing rather than an accident. Extortion, arbitrary charges, forced testing and documented officer sexual abuse recur across 2022–2024 with no non-discrimination law, no ministry access and NGOs working anonymously — the liability clause applies fully, since institutions are the perpetrators. Public attitudes are entirely negative, raising outing probability at every social encounter, while emergency care is documented as disrespectful. Unknowns (border screening, trans detention placement, minor-specific treatment) are open questions, not clearances. Absence of criminalisation and of recorded trans killings keeps this above the 0.15 tier; state-directed targeting with no working remedy keeps it well below 0.35.
